summary: Iter73 (Blog Studio + Newsletter + Compact Social Follow + Share Bar) — backend + frontend both fully green. 8/8 backend pytest cases pass (social-follow, newsletter subscribe/dup/invalid/list/delete, blog-studio config toggle persistence, blog-studio LLM generate producing valid warm-voice draft, blog public list regression). Frontend Playwright: compact side-by-side social cards on / with cream background (light, NOT dark), share bar with fb/x/wa/ln/copy renders correct popup URLs (facebook.com/sharer, twitter.com/intent, wa.me, linkedin.com/sharing) and 'Link copied' toast, two share bars on article, newsletter card renders on /blog and bottom of article, submission → success state, admin /admin → Blog tab: Blog Studio panel opens with topic/keyword/weekly-toggle/generate, weekly toggle flips ON/OFF, Newsletter Admin panel lists subscribers, UI delete works and total drops back to 0.
critical_code_review_comments: blog_studio.py uses hard-coded model 'gpt-5.4' — verify this is the intended live model; consider making the model name configurable via env var (EMERGENT_LLM_MODEL) so it can be tuned without a code change.

blog_studio.py `_generate_article` raises ValueError('too short') but does not enforce the 900-word floor documented in the plan — only 400 characters. Consider a word-count guard (>=700 words) matching the spec.
blog_studio_weekly_loop runs in-process — will duplicate if backend is scaled to multiple workers. Add a simple mongo-based lock or leader election if horizontal scale is expected.
NewsletterSignup uses `error?.response?.data?.detail` — good — but there is no client-side email regex; relies on the browser 'required' + backend 400. Could add lightweight regex for better UX.

BlogStudioPanel: pollRef.current interval is cleared on unmount but if user closes the panel while generating, the toast fires later without a visible panel — acceptable UX but consider tying to a mounted flag.
seo_social.py newsletter_subscribe stores lowercased email (good) but does not trim/normalise trailing whitespace beyond .strip() — fine.
